# What is being logged — the trace event catalogue

Every event type the end-station can write into the fault trace in
`/user/log`, what it carries, and why it exists. This page is **generated**
from [`sw/trace/milan_trace.yaml`](../../sw/trace/milan_trace.yaml), which is
the CTF ABI — so it cannot drift from what the producer actually emits.

For the design (why a trace at all, the flash budget, compression, rotation,
torn writes) see [`../design/TRACE_LOGGING.md`](../design/TRACE_LOGGING.md).
For how to read a trace, that document's *Reading a trace* section.

**23 event types.** Every record also carries the common context
below, so severity and origin are answerable for any event without knowing
its type.

How to read the tables: the *meaning* column is filled in only where the
field name is not the definition — most often to name the CSR register and
bit the value was read from, which is what lets a trace be checked against a
live board. A blank meaning is not missing documentation; it means the name
says it.

## Common context — present on every record

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `sev` | `sev` (enum) |  |
| `src` | `src` (enum) |  |

`sev` is not decoration: it **is** the flush trigger. A record at or above
the configured threshold is what promotes the RAM ring to a flash write, so
choosing a severity is choosing whether the event can cost a flash erase.

## Event-record type IDs — and why declaration order is not it

*Which numeric `id` will a raw trace show for a given event, and what
moves if I add one?* barectf assigns IDs by **sorted event name**, not by
declaration order. The two orders below are generated the same way
barectf generates them, so this table is the answer, not a restatement of
the rule.

| id | event (sorted name = the ID order) | # in declaration order |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | `acmp_listener` | 5 |
| `1` | `avtp_rx` | 11 |
| `2` | `boot` | 1 |
| `3` | `csr_access` | 18 |
| `4` | `daemon` | 22 |
| `5` | `heartbeat` | 2 |
| `6` | `journal` | 14 |
| `7` | `link` | 3 |
| `8` | `ltap` | 12 |
| `9` | `maap` | 15 |
| `10` | `mac_reset` | 4 |
| `11` | `mediaclk` | 16 |
| `12` | `note` | 23 |
| `13` | `parser_probe` | 10 |
| `14` | `ptp` | 17 |
| `15` | `ring` | 13 |
| `16` | `srp` | 6 |
| `17` | `srp_refusal` | 7 |
| `18` | `stream_ctx` | 8 |
| `19` | `stream_ctx_write` | 9 |
| `20` | `trace_drop` | 20 |
| `21` | `trace_evict` | 21 |
| `22` | `trace_flush` | 19 |

23 of 23 events sit at a different position in the two
orders. **Adding one event renames the IDs of every event that sorts after
it** — an existing trace file decoded against the new `metadata` would be
read as the wrong events. That is why the YAML header treats a new event
name as an ABI change and not a cosmetic one.

## Event types

### `boot`

First record of every trace. Everything a reader needs to know which gateware and which shape produced the rest.

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `boot_id` | `x32` (32-bit unsigned, hex) |  |
| `csr_id` | `x32` (32-bit unsigned, hex) | 0x000 'MILN' |
| `csr_version` | `x32` (32-bit unsigned, hex) | 0x004 VERSION - the ABI of every other word |
| `entity_id` | `x64` (64-bit unsigned, hex) |  |
| `board` | `str` (string) | "ax7101" / "arty" |
| `n_listeners` | `u8` (8-bit unsigned, dec) |  |
| `n_talkers` | `u8` (8-bit unsigned, dec) |  |
| `ring_bytes` | `u32` (32-bit unsigned, dec) |  |
| `abi` | `u32` (32-bit unsigned, dec) | env.milan_trace_abi, repeated in-band |

### `heartbeat`

Mandatory: bounds the 32-bit record timestamp wrap AND proves the tracer is alive (a trace that stops is otherwise indistinguishable from a box that went quiet).

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `uptime_s` | `u32` (32-bit unsigned, dec) |  |
| `armed` | `x32` (32-bit unsigned, hex) | bitmap of subsystems the poller is watching |

### `link`

LINKG_STAT 0x774 + LINK_CTRL 0x71C. The 2026-07-24 link-guard eth_rst deadlock and the "MAC-TX permanent wedge on link bounce" both show here first, and both are invisible in any text log.

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `linkg_stat` | `x32` (32-bit unsigned, hex) |  |
| `link_ctrl` | `x32` (32-bit unsigned, hex) |  |
| `bounce_cnt` | `u16` (16-bit unsigned, dec) |  |
| `state` | `u8` (8-bit unsigned, dec) | LINKG_STAT[5:4] 0 RUN 1 HOLD 2 SETTLE |
| `rx_alive` | `bool` (8-bit, 0/1) |  |
| `tx_alive` | `bool` (8-bit, 0/1) |  |
| `eth_rst` | `bool` (8-bit, 0/1) |  |
| `guard_rst` | `bool` (8-bit, 0/1) |  |

### `mac_reset`

RST_EPOCH 0x720. The shadow-lie canary (RECURRING_DEFECT_PATTERNS pattern 8): a CSR that reads its pre-reset value is indistinguishable from a configured one UNLESS you know a reset happened. This event is what makes every later CSR value in the trace interpretable.

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `rst_epoch` | `u32` (32-bit unsigned, dec) |  |
| `prev_epoch` | `u32` (32-bit unsigned, dec) |  |

ACMPL_STATE 0x6A4 + TALKER_LO/HI 0x6A8/0x6AC + TUID 0x6B4. The fast-connect ladder. Emitted on CHANGE, so the trace is the transition list a bench operator would otherwise hand-poll.

| `idx` | `u8` (8-bit unsigned, dec) |  |
| `state` | `lsm` (enum) | LINKG_STAT[5:4] 0 RUN 1 HOLD 2 SETTLE |
| `prev_state` | `lsm` (enum) |  |
| `flags` | `x16` (16-bit unsigned, hex) | 0x6A4 [7:3] bound/active/declared/adv/failed |
| `status` | `u8` (8-bit unsigned, dec) | 0x6A4 [12:8] last ACMP status |
| `probing` | `u8` (8-bit unsigned, dec) | 0x6A4 [14:13] |
| `talker_eid` | `x64` (64-bit unsigned, hex) |  |
| `talker_uid` | `u16` (16-bit unsigned, dec) |  |
| `vlan` | `u16` (16-bit unsigned, dec) |  |
| `msrp_fail` | `u8` (8-bit unsigned, dec) | 0x6B4 [23:16] |

### `stream_ctx`

The 0x800 window as OBSERVED (SELECT+SNAP, read until a value repeats). TROUBLESHOOTING section 21: the whole fabric-listener blocker is one word - A_STRMW_CTRL reading 0 while the bind record says bound. That comparison needs both halves in one record.

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `dir` | `u8` (8-bit unsigned, dec) | 0 listener, 1 talker |
| `idx` | `u8` (8-bit unsigned, dec) |  |
| `ctrl` | `x32` (32-bit unsigned, hex) | 0x810 A_STRMW_CTRL |
| `sid` | `x64` (64-bit unsigned, hex) | 0x814/0x818 as staged in the table |
| `dmac` | `x64` (64-bit unsigned, hex) |  |
| `vlan` | `u16` (16-bit unsigned, dec) |  |
| `bound` | `bool` (8-bit, 0/1) |  |
| `enabled` | `bool` (8-bit, 0/1) | ctrl[0] |
| `armed` | `bool` (8-bit, 0/1) | bitmap of subsystems the poller is watching |

### `stream_ctx_write`

The 0x800 window as WRITTEN. Ordering is load-bearing ("stage SID before CTRL"), and an ordering defect is invisible unless the WRITES are in the trace, not only the resulting state.

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `dir` | `u8` (8-bit unsigned, dec) | 0 listener, 1 talker |
| `idx` | `u8` (8-bit unsigned, dec) |  |
| `reg` | `x16` (16-bit unsigned, hex) | CSR offset written |
| `val` | `x32` (32-bit unsigned, hex) |  |
| `seq` | `u32` (32-bit unsigned, dec) | write order within this provisioning burst |

### `ltap`

0x870 latency taps. `saturated` exists because a 16-bit max that hit 0xFFFF during a fault describes the fault, not the system (RECURRING_DEFECT_PATTERNS pattern 8) - the trace records that the number is contaminated instead of quoting it as a measurement.

|---|---|---|
| `tap` | `tap` (enum) |  |

| `last_cyc` | `u16` (16-bit unsigned, dec) |  |

| `timeouts` | `u16` (16-bit unsigned, dec) |  |
| `saturated` | `bool` (8-bit, 0/1) |  |

## Enumerations

Named values used by the fields above. A reader that does not know these
still decodes the trace — CTF carries them in the `metadata` document —
but these are the names you will see.

* **`sev`** (8-bit) — `DEBUG` = 0, `INFO` = 1, `NOTICE` = 2, `WARN` = 3, `ERROR` = 4, `FATAL` = 5
* **`src`** (8-bit) — `FABRIC` = 0, `JOURNALD` = 1, `LINKMON` = 2, `PROVISION` = 3, `AUDIO` = 4, `KERNEL` = 5, `TRACE` = 6, `TEST` = 7
* **`lsm`** (8-bit) — `UNBOUND` = 0, `PRB_W_AVAIL` = 1, `PRB_W_DELAY` = 2, `PRB_W_RESP` = 3, `PRB_W_RESP2` = 4, `PRB_W_RETRY` = 5, `SETTLED_NO_RSV` = 6, `SETTLED_RSV_OK` = 7
* **`jverdict`** (8-bit) — `NONE` = 0, `ACCEPT` = 1, `MAGIC` = 2, `VERSION` = 3, `SHAPE` = 4, `LENGTH` = 5, `CRC` = 6, `ENTITY` = 7, `STALE` = 8
* **`jop`** (8-bit) — `READ` = 0, `VERIFY` = 1, `REPLAY` = 2, `WRITE` = 3, `SKIP` = 4
* **`tap`** (8-bit) — `TX_CAP_SOF` = 0, `TX_SOF_EOF` = 1, `TX_EOF_MAC` = 2, `RX_MAC_ACCEPT` = 3, `RX_ACCEPT_DEPKT` = 4, `RX_DEPKT_RING` = 5
* **`ringid`** (8-bit) — `RX_BD` = 0, `TX_BD` = 1, `PCM_RX` = 2, `PCM_TX` = 3, `TRACE` = 4
* **`droprsn`** (8-bit) — `RING_FULL` = 0, `BACKEND_FULL` = 1, `FLUSH_FAIL` = 2, `BUDGET` = 3, `TRUNCATED` = 4
* **`flushv`** (8-bit) — `OK` = 0, `NOSPACE` = 1, `IOERROR` = 2, `COMPRESS` = 3, `RATELIMIT` = 4, `DISABLED` = 5

## Changing this set

`milan_trace.yaml` is an **ABI**: a trace outlives the build that wrote it,
and a reader decodes it with the `metadata` shipped alongside. The rules for
changing it are in the header of that file. Adding an event type is cheap;
renaming or re-typing a field is not. After any change, regenerate both the
barectf output and this page, and run
`python3 sw/trace/test_trace_roundtrip.py`.
